summary.headline: One Point One Solutions Q2 FY27 revenue rose about 10.5% QoQ to Rs 174.96 crore, with EBITDA margin of 25.9% and PAT of Rs 18.41 crore.
summary.overview: Management reported Q2 FY27 revenue from operations of Rs 174.96 crore, up about 10.5% QoQ, with EBITDA of Rs 45.32 crore and a 25.9% margin (about 100 bps sequential improvement). PAT rose to Rs 18.41 crore. H1 FY27 revenue was Rs 333.28 crore and H1 EBITDA Rs 84.69 crore (25.4% margin). Management attributed growth to organic expansion, new accounts, renewals and AI-led cross-selling, and highlighted new multi-year mandates in India, Costa Rica and North America. The call was mostly qualitative; many answers on capex, CWIP, AI revenue and guidance were vague.

financial_highlights.change: about 10.5% QoQ; CFO also cited 147% YoY, which appears to be a transcription error and is unverified
15.1% QoQ vs Rs 39.38 crore in Q1 FY27; 10.6% YoY as stated
about 100 bps QoQ improvement; Q2 FY26 margin cited as 30.6% by analyst
12.9% QoQ vs Rs 16.31 crore in Q1 FY27; 26.1% YoY as stated

financial_highlights.value: Rs 54 crore (analyst figure, confirmed after correction from Rs 1,100 crore)
financial_highlights.change: up from Rs 11 crore per analyst

segments.name: Resolute (AI platform, subsidiary 1.1 Technologies Labs)
segments.commentary: 14 deployments across 7 enterprise clients in five months since launch, spanning insurance, aviation, banking, automotive and digital assets. Revenue contribution was not disclosed; management plans to segregate Resolute revenue in future quarters.

segments.name: Clariva (AI medical record summarisation, North America)
segments.commentary: Processing over 100,000 records per month with turnaround under three days and accuracy up to 99.7%, per management. No revenue figure given.

segments.name: Core CX / BPM operations
segments.commentary: Pricing is time-and-material or transaction-based for non-Resolute business; Resolute uses outcome-linked consumption pricing with a one-time integration fee and no platform or licence fee.

guidance_outlook: Management said H2 FY27 revenue run-rate should be similar to the last two quarters; it described contracts as annuity-like, multi-year (3-5 years), and said revenue should not decline QoQ.
Management guided to at least 15-20% YoY growth for next year, stating this as a strategy focus and noting acquisitions could add upside.
Management said Rs 2,000 crore revenue target until FY30 remains intact, with the company possibly going beyond it in FY27 on organic growth plus any acquisitions.
Management said it is evaluating acquisitions, with no timeline given.
Management said AI-linked deployments will be disclosed for financial impact once they become material to the consolidated business.
Management did not quantify capex for the current or next fiscal year.
capex_capacity: Capitalised AI platform development (CWIP) of more than Rs 80 crore on the books; management said the product is still in development and depreciation will begin once it is completed and revenue is visible, expected in the coming quarter(s).
Further investment is being made in the AI platform this quarter; no capex quantum for FY27 or FY28 was provided.

Stake increase in a subsidiary via conversion of loans and advances into equity; analyst cited about Rs 25 crore (Rs 21 crore loan plus Rs 4 crore advance) for an additional 2.75% stake. Management declined to disclose valuation.
Company described itself as debt-free except for one term loan taken for an acquisition at about 9% cost; analyst figures indicated short-term borrowings of about Rs 54 crore.
demand_pricing: New mandates: a three-year enterprise mandate with a large US security depository (omni-channel CX, CCaaS, CRM, ticketing, email automation); a Costa Rica national training institute contract worth about $10.8 million over four years (about $2.7 million annual); an India customer-experience centre of excellence mandate from a leading power utility, cited as Rs 39.32 crore; a three-year CX mandate with VRL Logistics.
Management said the Resolute pipeline is strong for the year, with new deployments going live and cross-selling of products such as Ombia, Frequency, NET and RightFIT.
Ombia live agent-based bots more than tripled in three months; deployed at India's largest private life insurer across seven Indian languages.
Insurance deployment results cited: 4x voice audit coverage, 50% faster agent feedback, about 24% lower AHT, and a 79-point rise in customer satisfaction.
Management said AI deals are bundled with manpower work, which it expects to lift margins over time.
Management said it is focusing on North America for acquisitions and geographic growth.

qa_highlights.question: What is the H2 outlook and can it be converted into numbers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the outlook is clear and it has a promising start from the first two quarters, but declined to give a numerical range. It is continuing the same strategy of growing within existing accounts.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Rs 80 crore+ CWIP and the capex guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: The CWIP relates to the AI platform still in development; further spend continues this quarter, revenue is expected within coming quarters, and depreciation starts on completion. No capex quantum was given.

qa_highlights.question: Is the AI platform sector-agnostic, and how was Clariva trained?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the platform is industry-agnostic and deployed in aviation, automotive, life insurance and banking. Clariva is built on about two decades of manual medical record work and is fine-tuned with RLHF.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the subsidiary stake increased and what is its valuation?
qa_highlights.answer: Loans and advances were converted into equity to raise the parent's stake; management declined to disclose valuation, saying it would be revealed later and the company is expected to be worth more than the carrying value.

qa_highlights.question: What is Resolute's revenue contribution and pricing model?
qa_highlights.answer: Revenue is not disclosed separately and will be segregated in future quarters. Resolute uses no platform or licence fee; it charges a one-time integration and deployment fee plus consumption based on resolutions. Rest of the business is T&M or transaction-based.

qa_highlights.question: Why did operating margin fall year on year and what is steady-state margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the YoY decline (from 30.6% to 25.9%) to a one-month acquisition impact in the prior-year base and said margins have held near 25% for the last two quarters; no steady-state figure was given.

qa_highlights.question: What growth guidance is there for next year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is looking at at least 15-20% YoY growth, with acquisitions as possible upside, but said it preferred to focus on the current year.

risks_watch: Capitalised AI platform (CWIP over Rs 80 crore) has not yet begun depreciation; timing of revenue and amortisation could affect future margins.
Resolute revenue is not disclosed separately, so the contribution of AI platform revenue is not visible yet.
Management's statements on the acquisition impact on margins and the sustainability of the Rs 2,000 crore target were unclear; the analyst's figures on borrowings and the YoY base need confirmation.
Subsidiary valuation and stake-increase rationale were not disclosed.
Q2 transcript contains transcription errors; key figures such as YoY growth, borrowings and deal values should be checked against the filed results.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on growth, deal wins and AI traction, but evasive on specifics: it declined to give H2 numbers, capex quantum, Resolute revenue, subsidiary valuation and steady-state margins.
key_quotes: Our business is not a project based business it's an annuity based business and it's a month on month revenue generation.
we have attached ourselves to the end customer journey outcome or resolution that we are providing
We are seeing adoption move beyond individual use cases with existing customers adding workflows and new deployments progressing into live enterprise environments.

growth.why: Management guided to at least 15-20% YoY growth for next year, backed by new multi-year mandates (Costa Rica ~$10.8m over four years, a Rs 39.32 crore utility CoE, US and VRL deals) and AI cross-selling, but no quantified capacity or capex was given and the call was largely qualitative.

rows.label: Margin expansion

rows.label: Volume growth

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Management did not quantify capex for the current or next fiscal year; the business is asset-light with a Rs 80 crore+ CWIP AI platform still in development, and debt is limited to one term loan at about 9% plus short-term borrowings of about Rs 54 crore.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Management said the AI platform (CWIP above Rs 80 crore) will generate revenue very soon and depreciation starts on completion, with further spend this quarter; no launch date was specified.

rows.label: New multi-year mandates (Costa Rica, utility CoE, US, VRL)
rows.why: Costa Rica contract about $10.8m over four years (about $2.7m a year), a Rs 39.32 crore utility CoE mandate and a three-year VRL CX mandate add to the annuity-like, 3-5 year book.

rows.label: North America focus for acquisitions and growth
rows.why: Management is focusing on North America for acquisitions and geographic growth, but evaluating deals with no timeline; Clariva already processes over 100,000 records per month there.

tone.note: Management was confident on growth, deal wins, AI traction and margin stability near 25%, but evasive on H2 numbers, capex quantum, Resolute revenue, subsidiary valuation and steady-state margin; analysts pushed on these gaps and on the YoY base and borrowings.
